history.heading: Scattered islands
paragraphs: The United States Minor Outlying Islands are nine small, remote islands and atolls in the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean: Baker Island, Howland Island, Jarvis Island, Johnston Atoll, Kingman Reef, Midway Atoll, Palmyra Atoll, Wake Island and Navassa Island.

Many were claimed in the 19th century under the Guano Islands Act of 1856, which allowed US citizens to take possession of uninhabited islands with deposits of bird guano used as fertiliser. Midway Atoll was the site of the decisive 1942 Battle of Midway, a turning point in the Pacific War. Howland Island was Amelia Earhart's destination when she disappeared in 1937. Johnston Atoll was used for nuclear tests and chemical weapons disposal.

culture.heading: No permanent population
paragraphs: None of the islands has a permanent population. Wake Island hosts US military personnel and contractors, and Midway and Palmyra have small staffs of wildlife officials and researchers.

politics.heading: US territories
paragraphs: The islands are unincorporated territories administered by US agencies, mainly the Fish and Wildlife Service and the military. Most are part of the Pacific Remote Islands Marine National Monument. Navassa Island is claimed by Haiti, and Wake Island is claimed by the Marshall Islands.

economy.heading: Conservation
paragraphs: There is no economic activity. The islands are important wildlife refuges, home to millions of seabirds, sea turtles and pristine coral reefs. The currency, where used, is the US dollar.
